messages:
infra-alert-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED maya (oncall) for incident 2234567890 — interregion health ring flap detected. Symptoms: rapid health-check toggles between us-east <-> us-west <-> eu, causing fallback churn and traffic oscillation. Auto-fallback triggered to variant small-quantized-1 in eu then bounced back.
maya (oncall): I'm on it. could someone confirm if any customer-facing errors reported?
trent (sre): seeing ~30% of requests getting 503s during spikes on the proxy logs. looks correlated to the routing decisions changing every 20-40s.
laura (eng-runtime): ack. RT logs show KV-cache misses and stale model-variant mismatches when fallback flips. model tracer shows requests hitting different quant levels mid-session.
maya (oncall): paging sequence — trent you own triage, laura you own runtime mitigation. ops-shift please hold customer comms. I'll escalate if pd response needed.
pagerduty-bot: Incident created: INC-2234567890. Priority: P1. Escalation schedule engaged.
ops-shift: noted, drafting a short blurb for affected customers. nothing committed yet.
trent (sre): quick dump of probe timings: `probe -> us-east (ok) 12s, us-west (fail) 8s, eu (ok) 6s` then flip to `us-east fail -> us-west ok` within 30s. looks like probe timeouts + synchronized probe intervals.
laura (eng-runtime): that matches: our health-check backoffs are identical across regions (30s) and no jitter. if probes hit at similar times we can get cascading failover.
maya (oncall): mitigation idea 1: temporarily increase probe tolerance and add jitter to health-checks. mitigation idea 2: disable cross-region fallback policy to prefer local region until stability. which do we want first?
trent (sre): do both. but first action: disable automatic fallback policy so we stop routing churn. I can flip policy flag in routing control.
laura (eng-runtime): I'll pin model variant to stable-replica for the problematic customer-facing route so we avoid variant mismatches while routing policy is toggled.
maya (oncall): trent, go ahead. laura, do the pin. ops-shift, prepare message: short, non-technical note + ETA for update.
trent (sre): changing routing.flag.auto_fallback = false -> true/false?? executing: `rdctl route update --name default-fallback --auto-fallback=false --reason "mitigate ring-flap"`
ops-shift: draft ready: "We're seeing transient routing instability across regions which may cause brief errors for some customers. We're applying temporary routing safeguards and will update in 30 minutes. No data loss expected." want me to send?
maya (oncall): yes send after laura confirms the variant pin completed.
laura (eng-runtime): applying variant pin: `rdctl model pin --route default --model stable-replica --duration 60m --note "pin during interregion flap"` -> success. TTL 60m.
trent (sre): routing flag flipped. monitoring logs. initial metrics: 503 rate down from 30% -> 7% in 2 mins. latency still slightly elevated.
maya (oncall): ops-shift send the blurb now. I'll add a brief on-call note.
ops-shift: sent to customers affected by default route (approx 12 orgs). pasted here: "We have applied temporary routing safeguards to reduce request churn; minor disruptions may persist for up to 60 minutes. We'll follow up with a technical summary."
trent (sre): added throttling to fallback decisions to avoid immediate subsequent flips: `routing.policy.fallback_min_interval=120s` deployed to control plane.
laura (eng-runtime): also disabled synchronized probe schedule and added jitter: `health.probe.jitter=20s` and increased fail threshold from 2->4.
maya (oncall): good. can we confirm customer sessions that hit mixed-variant are being remediated?
trent (sre): tracing shows session continuity restored for 95% of sampled sessions. a handful still show KV-cache mismatch — investigating one flow now.
laura (eng-runtime): found a small race: when routing switch happens mid-stream we rehydrate KV from different quant path; adding guard to reject variant-change-mid-session for now. patch queued, will hotfix if needed.
maya (oncall): PD update: escalation not needed right now. will keep on-call chain open until stability 30m.
pagerduty-bot: INC-2234567890 status: acknowledged, responders: maya (oncall), trent (sre), laura (eng-runtime).
trent (sre): follow-up: traffic normalized, cross-region failover suppressed, probe jitter appears effective. metrics: fallback count per minute dropped from 18 -> 1.
ops-shift: customers asked for postmortem — I'll collect initial timeline.
laura (eng-runtime): will push a small guard to production: `if session.active and proposed_variant != current_variant -> reject routing-change until session end` rolling 5 instances now.
maya (oncall): ETA on full rollback of mitigations? we should keep pin + fallback guard for 60m then reassess.
trent (sre): agreed. set reminder for 60m to re-evaluate flags and remove pins.
ops-shift: sending follow-up update to customers: "We’ve applied mitigations and are monitoring. We’ll provide a technical postmortem within 24 hours."
maya (oncall): thumbs. postmortem owners: trent (timeline + infra), laura (runtime root cause + fix), ops-shift (customer comms). I'll be lead reviewer.
trent (sre): initial root cause hypothesis: synchronized health-check schedules + low probe tolerance created a ring of transient failures; combined with aggressive auto-fallback and absence of variant-change guards led to session instability.
laura (eng-runtime): agree. long-term actions: add probe jitter by default, require min fallback hold time, and add variant-change atomicity in runtime. I'll open PRs for each.
maya (oncall): closing notes: incident downgraded to P2 monitoring. keep eyes on traces for next 2 hours. good job everyone :heart: 
infra-alert-bot: Incident 2234567890 updated: severity -> P2, handlers: maya (oncall).
